# leg merged INTO the linux leg below — ONE sharded PTY/CLI integration
  # job on ubuntu-24.04-arm that now also carries the per-shard coverage +
  # dart-json/junit reporting the gate consumes. A PR validation's PTY legs
  # never wait on fa-m5-1; hosted macOS (10x minute cost) is never used.
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  pty-integration-linux:
    # THE PR PTY/CLI integration leg (gh-1005: the former mac leg merged in;
    # before that, issue #931 part 2 sharded ONE ~40-min job into 3
    # duration-balanced shards — scripts/test_integration_shards.json,
    # file-level units). New integration-tagged files bin-pack in at runtime
    # (shard_files.py --tags integration), so a PR adding one never
    # silently skips it. Explicit --concurrency=4 bounds in-suite
    # parallelism (part 3.3 — package:test forbids `concurrency` in
    # dart_test.yaml tag overrides, so the knob lives here; it bounds
    # concurrent live-provider tests PER JOB — the rate-limit rationale is
    # documented on the llm tag in dart_test.yaml).
    # Per-shard coverage artifacts merge in pty-coverage-gate —
    # a single shard's ratchet would see partial lib/src/cli coverage
    # and false-regress. Each shard also emits the dart json
    # file-reporter: junit feeds rebalancing/budget-tightening PRs, the
    # raw json feeds the #928 duration gate (pty-coverage-gate below).
    # gh-1300: needs the once-per-run AOT build; FA_BIN points every CLI
    # spawn (PTY harness + headless helpers) at the prebuilt binary.
    needs: [release-pending, release-dedupe, fa-aot-build]
    # gh-1551: an empty schedule tick (no commits since the last v* tag)
    # skips this leg — the release-pending pre-check decides.
    if: needs.release-pending.outputs.pending == 'true' && needs.release-dedupe.outputs.dedupe != 'true'
    name: PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04-arm
    # 40 > 30: the leg now carries the coverage + file-reporter overhead the
    # old mac leg had (the coverage-free linux twin never paid it) and arm64
    # Graviton cores run somewhat slower than the M-series minis did — margin
    # without stretching the watchdog much.
    timeout-minutes: 40
    permissions:
      contents: read
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        shard: [0, 1, 2]
    env:
      # Secret shape (review 2026-09-23): this is the pull_request-time leg
      # that receives real provider secrets. GitHub withholds secrets from
      # forks, so external contributions never see them — but every
      # SAME-REPO branch runs this suite with the keys in its process
      # environment before human review (this repo's agent-authored-branch
      # model). The marginal escalation vs the nightly (same suites, same
      # keys, post-merge on main) is small and the watchdog already hands
      # RELEASE_PAT to same-repo PRs; documented here so the assumption is
      # explicit, not implicit.
      #
      # The live-provider legs (unlocked by these keys) load extra
      # lib/src/cli surface into the coverage measurement, so a no-key run
      # measures a DIFFERENT — lower-numbered — value; missing keys (forks)
      # self-skip those legs gracefully and the gate stays honest either
      # way.
      OPENROUTER_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
      ANTHROPIC_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.ANTHROPIC_API_KEY }}
      GOOGLE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.GOOGLE_API_KEY }}
      OLLAMA_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OLLAMA_API_KEY }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable
      - run: dart pub get

      - name: Native-assets hook cache
        uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0
        with:
          path: .dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared
          key: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('pubspec.lock') }}
          restore-keys: hooks-shared-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      # gh-1300: the AOT binary built once per run by fa-aot-build. The
      # guard FAILS the shard loudly if the artifact is missing or dead —
      # a silent JIT fallback would hide the optimization from AC1's
      # before/after numbers.
      - uses: ./.github/actions/sqlite3-native-assets-prewarm
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@9000827ccba6bdab643e8b6fd33ac0654aef8333 # v8.0.2
        with:
          name: fa-aot-bin
          path: fa-local/bundle
      # Artifact zips do NOT preserve the exec bit (download-artifact
      # README: "post-download the file is no longer guaranteed to be set
      # as an executable"). Run 37446280743: `test -x` below failed
      # silently ~20 ms in on EVERY shard — the gate went red before a
      # single test ran. Restore the mode the build job shipped; the
      # smoke below still verifies the restored binary is executable and
      # boots (never a silent JIT fallback). Content integrity is not
      # affected: download-artifact digest-validates (digest-mismatch:
      # error default), so this chmod only ever touches the verified
      # bundle the fa-aot-build job produced.
      - name: Restore exec bit (artifact zips drop permissions)
        run: chmod +x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
      - name: Smoke the AOT binary (fail loud, never JIT-fallback)
        run: |
          test -x fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          ./fa-local/bundle/bin/fa --version
      - name: dart test --tags integration (linux, shard ${{ matrix.shard }}/3)
        env:
          # gh-1300 FA_BIN seam: every CLI spawn (pty_harness + the
          # headless helpers via faCliCommand) runs the AOT binary —
          # ~1 s per spawn instead of the JIT VM+CFE compile (~30 s on
          # loaded ARM runners). Per-test isolation is unchanged.
          FA_BIN: ${{ github.workspace }}/fa-local/bundle/bin/fa
          # Issue #1391: stretch every PTY-harness wait budget 2x on this
          # merge-blocking leg. SM dispatch waves pack the hosted-arm pool
          # (refresh waves supersede PR heads mid-run), and drilled reds
          # are all single tests popping quiet-runner budgets inside
          # otherwise-green 60-70-test shards. Local runs and the nightly
          # leave the var unset and keep the exact legacy budgets (the
          # nightly's unsupervised verdicts feed quarantine decisions).
          FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE: '2'
        run: |
          # gh-1199 AC1: --exclude-tag llm keeps every live-provider file
          # out of the merge-blocking selection (manifest unit AND runtime
          # bin-pack); --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm is the dart-test
          # backstop. AC6: the quarantine filter drops flake-quarantined
          # files (scripts/test_quarantine.json) pending their fix PRs.
          targets=$(python3 scripts/shard_files.py scripts/test_integration_shards.json ${{ matrix.shard }} --tags integration --exclude browser_ext --exclude-tag llm | python3 scripts/apply_quarantine.py)
          echo "shard targets: $targets"
          if [ -z "$targets" ]; then
            echo "shard fully quarantined — nothing to run"
            exit 0
          fi
          mkdir -p build/test-results
          dart test --tags integration --exclude-tags browser-ext,llm \
            --concurrency=4 \
            --coverage=coverage \
            --file-reporter="json:build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json" \
            $targets
      # The file-reporter writes the json even on a RED leg — convert +
      # upload must not be chained into the failing step (#928 review):
      # timing evidence is exactly what red runs need to keep.
      - name: junit durations (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})
        if: always()
        run: >-
          python3 scripts/junit_from_dart_json.py
          build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
      # Raw dart json for the #928 duration gate (per-test spans incl. suite
      # paths); junit is the human/rebalancer-facing form of the same data.
      # Upload MUST stay on the current upload-artifact line (gh-995): the
      # gate's download-artifact v8 digest-validates every download, so an
      # old-line upload digest-mismatches and the shard merge loses its
      # report (test/gh995_artifact_action_pins_test.dart pins the pin).
      #
      # gh-1412: each evidence upload carries a one-shot retry (the step
      # right after it, same pinned action). The gh-1412 validation run
      # 37807820733 red'd a shard whose 68 tests ALL passed on a single
      # transient `Failed to FinalizeArtifact: ECONNRESET` from GitHub's
      # blob storage — the aggregate gate followed and the merge aborted.
      # The retry re-runs the SAME action with overwrite:true (a failed
      # attempt leaves the artifact half-registered — without overwrite the
      # retry dies on "already exists"); a genuinely dead endpoint still
      # fails the shard loudly, and the retries stay if: always()-reachable
      # so red legs keep their evidence. Guarded by
      # test/ci_pty_artifact_upload_retry_guard_test.dart.
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_json
        if: always()
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          # gh-2200: rerun --failed never fires the gh-1412 retry (the
          # first attempt's upload succeeded), so without this the rerun
          # uploads a SECOND same-named artifact and download-artifact
          # pattern-mode resolves the STALE previous-attempt report — the
          # pty-coverage-gate then merges a truncated shard json and
          # phantom-fails "budgeted suite did not run" (run 43752856871
          # attempt 2). The latest attempt's evidence must win.
          overwrite: true
      - name: Retry integration-json upload (transient blob-storage reset, gh-1412)
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        if: always() && steps.upload_integration_json.outcome == 'failure'
        with:
          name: integration-json-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.json
          retention-days: 2
          overwrite: true
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        id: upload_integration_junit
        if: always()
        with:
          name: junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}
          path: build/test-results/junit-integration-shard-${{ matrix.shard }}.xml
          retention-days: 7
          # gh-2200: same rerun-idempotency as upload_integration_json —
          # a rerun attempt must REPLACE its previous attempt's artifact,

TITLE: PTY integration CI: dart VM isolate spawn/check-in stall — Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in (36+ min hang, upstream dart-lang/sdk class)
LABELS: []

=== BODY ===
## What happened

`PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)`, run 43151400571 (2026-11-12, PR #2121): all **81 tests in the shard passed in ~30 s** (03:57:30 → 03:57:57), then the leg hung for **36+ minutes** until the run was superseded:

- 03:57:58 — coverage collection starts (`package:coverage collect → getSourceReport`, stack in the log);
- 03:58:09 → 04:34:49 — the log fills with **4,400 lines** of `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`, attempts reaching **#2210** (~2 lines/second);
- the run was cancelled by a superseding push; post-cancel cleanup terminated orphan `dart:concatenat` / `dart:dartdev_ao` processes.

Sibling evidence on IDENTICAL content, same image (`macos-26-arm64` image `20261102.0473.1` in all cases), same SDKs:

- run 43147985274 (30 min earlier): all three PTY shards green in **~2.5 min** each;
- run 43155863851 (35 min later, same head content): PTY shard 2 green in the normal envelope;
- a full `--update-goldens` capture on the same hosted pool rendered 396 baselines **byte-identical** minutes after the hang.

## Root cause — upstream, not our harness

`Attempt:N waiting for isolate <name> to check in` is a **Dart VM-internal isolate spawn/check-in handshake** retry loop (the string is compiled into `dartaotruntime` / `flutter_tester`). The stalled isolate here is named `_waitForExitCode` — package:test_core's helper isolate that waits for a suite isolate's exit code.

Known upstream class, open since 2021:

- dart-lang/sdk#45771 — `Attempt:xxx waiting for isolate vm-isolate to check in` (dart migrate)
- dart-lang/sdk#46255 — `Attempt:11 waiting for isolate vm-isolate to check in`
- flutter/flutter#80739 — same signature

We cannot fix the VM handshake from this repo. What we CAN decide, with eyes open:

1. Nothing (accept rare multi-minute burns; they self-heal on retry) — status quo.
2. A bounded wait around the coverage-bearing `dart test` legs so a stall fails fast instead of zombie-ing the runner pool — rejected as a band-aid for now per owner call; if it recurs at cost, revisit as a deliberate policy.
3. Investigate whether the stall correlates with coverage collection load (`getSourceReport` in flight when the handshake starves) — e.g. run one shard with `--coverage` off as a data point.

## Evidence pointers

- red job log: run 43151400571, job 130961615719 (line ~547 for the attempt storm, ~530 for the coverage stack)
- green siblings: run 43147985274 jobs 130950779014.., run 43155863851 (PTY shard 2)
- identical-image proof: all three jobs report `Image: macos-26-arm64 / Version: 20261102.0473.1`

content.thinking:
No exit() calls in the frozen tests. ssh_shift_gate's frozen test had JUST started (t=30401, 2 seconds before the crash) — it spawns its EchoMock HTTP server and then `FaCliHarness.spawn` → fork of the runner process.

NOW — WAIT. THE HTTP SERVER! `_EchoMock` binds 127.0.0.1 on an EPHEMERAL port. `spawnFa` → `PseudoTerminal.start` → **fork()** → the child inherits the runner's LISTEN SOCKET fd (no CLOEXEC) → execve into fa → fa inherits the mock's listen socket... no impact on parent.

Hmm. But ALSO: `dart test`'s VM SERVICE websocket fd is inherited by every fa child. STILL no parent-side close.

Let me take stock and think about what fix I can own IN THIS REPO:

**Established facts:**
1. The failing leg is a known recurring hang class (#212): the `dart test` process wedges at (or racing) shutdown when a pty2 `_waitForExitCode` isolate is blocked in native `waitpid` on a still-alive PTY child. 10+ occurrences. Same terminal signature. Killed by the 40-min watchdog; reds the Quality gate; **blocks the v1.0.735 release publish entirely**.
2. pty2's `_waitForExitCode` isolate can NEVER be killed by the VM while in native waitpid. The ONLY way to free it: the PTY child must die.
3. Our harness's `close()`/`hardKill()` GIVE UP after 5 s (onTimeout: -1) leaving fa alive; `tui_protype_snapshot_test.dart`'s tearDown calls `pty.kill()` WITHOUT awaiting exit — a hot CI exit can beat the child's death → wedge at exit-time isolate check-in (matches the 11-12 mac run where ALL tests passed and the process STILL wedged at exit).
4. In today's run, the shutdown began MID-RUN (12 suites queued/3 in flight) — triggered by the coverage websocket closing ("Service connection disposed"). The mid-run shutdown then wedged on the 3 in-flight suites' live PTY children. (The websocket-close trigger itself remains unproven from available evidence — but it ALSO matches the VM-shutdown class: once the VM starts exiting, the service closes connections. And a shutdown trigger that makes the VM exit mid-run could be the SAME VM stall class — e.g. a fork/ffi-related runtime stall in the service isolate. What I can fix: make the suite teardown NOT leave live PTY children, and make the harness's exits deterministic.)

**What can we actually fix in-repo?**

Fix A (deterministic child death — the load-bearing fix):
- `FaCliHarness.close()`/`hardKill()`: SIGTERM → bounded wait → **SIGKILL escalation** → await exitCode (bounded) → cancel subscription. Never return while the child lives. If SIGKILL + await still can't reap within budget → throw (fail the test loudly instead of silently leaking a child that wedges the VM at exit).
- `tui_protype_snapshot_test.dart` tearDown: await the exit (kill + bounded await with SIGKILL escalation).

Fix B (grandchildren): `pty.kill()` signals only the fa PID. If fa is SIGKILLed while its own children live, the children hold the PTY slave → `_readUntilExit`'s poll loop: process dead → returns null anyway (pty2 checks `_isProcessDead`). So grandchildren do NOT wedge the pty2 isolates. Fine.

Fix C (the mid-run VM-service close → shutdown): out of our control (VM-internal; #212 owner call was "do nothing / revisit"). BUT we CAN shrink the blast radius: the mid-run shutdown wedge happens because in-flight suites hold live fa children. A defensive measure at the DART-TEST level isn't available... but hmm — can we make pty2's waitpid isolates NON-blocking? Not without replacing pty2 (vendor?). Is pty2 vendored? `vendor/xterm` is. pty2 comes from pub. We could vendor-patch pty2... too invasive for this fix.

Hmm wait — actually, let me reconsider. There IS one more repo-side mitigation for the shutdown-wedge: **make the fa children die IMMEDIATELY when their test finishes even on unexpected paths — an `addTearDown` that hard-kills in every suite.** The harness ALREADY registers `addTearDown(harness.close)` in most tests. The gap: close()'s 5s give-up. Fixing close() closes that gap for mid-flight SIGTERM-ignored fa's... but NOT for the in-flight suites at the moment the VM service died mid-test (shell_job was 4 SECONDS into an 8-minute test — its fa was alive mid-test BY DESIGN; the shutdown wedged regardless of teardown because the shutdown KILLED the suite isolates without running their tearDowns!).

Hmm — that's the mid-run wedge: Engine catches the unexpected error → closes platforms → `isolate.kill` on suite isolates (cleanupCallbacks) → **tearDowns never run** → live fa children never killed → their pty2 waitpid isolates wedge the VM exit FOREVER.

So to actually stop the 39-minute hang for the MID-RUN shutdown case, we need the PTY child to die when the SUITE ISOLATE dies — impossible from Dart (isolate.kill is immediate, no handlers)... UNLESS the PTY child dies when the runner process dies — which is exactly the wedge (the runner process can't die because of the waitpid isolate).

**THE REAL FIX, THEN: make the pty2 waitpid isolate OBSOLETE or make sure the VM doesn't wait on it at exit.** Options:

1. **Switch the harness to `PollingPseudoTerminal`** — pty2 has it? I saw `BlockingPseudoTerminal` and the comment mentions "PollingPseudoTerminal (better suited for flutter debug mode)". Let me check: `pty.dart` exports... In 0.5.7 lib/src/pty.dart there's BlockingPseudoTerminal; where's Polling? Let me grep pty2 for PollingPseudoTerminal. If it exists and is non-blocking (poll loop on the event loop instead of isolates), the wedge disappears: no spawned isolates at all. That's a ONE-LINE-ISH change in pty_harness.dart — IF pty2 exposes it.

2. **Kill fa from the harness via a "dead man's switch"**: spawn fa with a watchdog — e.g., fa itself exits when its stdin closes... over PTY, stdin IS the pty. When the runner process dies, the pty master closes → the kernel sends SIGHUP to the session leader (fa is the session leader — TIOCSCTY + setsid) → **fa gets SIGHUP automatically when the master closes!** But the wedge: the master fd only closes when the read isolate's free() runs... which doesn't happen because the VM is wedged. CIRCULAR.

3. **pty.kill() escalation in close() (Fix A)** — fixes the ALL-PASED-exit-race class (the 11-12 mac trace, the tui_protype tearDown) — the MOST COMMON form (#212's original occurrence had all tests green!). The mid-run form (today) is rarer.

4. **Bound the whole thing at CI**: the ci.yml comment in #212 rejected a wrapper timeout ("band-aid per owner call") — so NOT that.

Let me check option 1 — does pty2 0.5.7 expose a polling terminal?

So the in-repo fixes available:

**Fix 1 (primary): hard-kill escalation + awaited exit in the harness.**
- `FaCliHarness.close()`: `pty.kill()` (SIGTERM+SIGHUP) → await exitCode ≤5s → if still alive: `pty.kill(ProcessSignal.sigkill)` → await exitCode ≤5s → if STILL alive: throw a loud error (a leaked fa would wedge the VM at exit — better to fail THIS test than zombie the whole leg).
- `FaCliHarness.hardKill()`: same shape (SIGKILL first, then await).
- `tui_protype_snapshot_test.dart` tearDown: `pty?.kill()` → await exitCode bounded, escalate to SIGKILL, await. (The 11-12 trace = all-green exit race → exactly this file's tearDown killing `dart run` without awaiting.)

Wait — but does awaiting the exit in tearDown actually prevent the exit-time wedge? The wedge needs `waitpid` to never return. If the harness awaits `pty.exitCode` (the pty2 future — completed by the `_waitForExitCode` isolate AFTER waitpid returns), then by the time the suite ends, the child is reaped and the isolate has EXITED (it sends the exit code, then its event loop finishes — the isolate dies naturally a moment later). One subtlety: after sending the exit code, the `_waitForExitCode` isolate ends — quick. The `_readUntilExit` isolate ends when read() returns null (POLLHUP/process-dead check every 100ms) — also quick, AND `free()` closes the master. So: awaiting exitCode (with SIGKILL escalation) guarantees BOTH isolates drain within ~100-200ms of the child's death. THE WEDGE DISAPEARS for teardown-time.

**Fix 2 (mid-run shutdown blast radius): can't stop the VM-service close, but I CAN stop the permanent wedge even when teardowns never run.** Hmm — how? Can the HARNESS arrange that at spawn time? YES — **a grandchild-side watchdog**: spawn fa via a tiny supervisor that exits when its PARENT (the runner) dies: `setsid` breaks parent-death signaling (the child is reparented to init, NOT killed). pty2's setsid defeats PR_SET_PDEATHSIG... # Root Cause Analysis — gh-2208 `[ci-red] v1.0.735 failed` (Quality gate)

## Root Cause Analysis

**Bug**: The `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` CI leg hung for 39 minutes after its
tests had already run, was killed by the 40-minute job watchdog, and red'd the aggregate
Quality gate — which blocked the `v1.0.735` release publish entirely (tag runs are the only
publish trigger; run 43835937617, sha 976ec46e).

**Root cause** (three linked layers):

1. **The terminal wedge (repo-owned)** — the `dart test` process cannot exit while any
   `package:pty2` PTY child is still alive. pty2's `BlockingPseudoTerminal` spawns an
   isolate per PTY running `_waitForExitCode` (pty2-0.5.7 `lib/src/pty.dart`), which blocks
   in a native FFI `waitpid(pid, 0)` with no timeout. A native-blocked isolate can neither
   reach a safepoint nor answer the VM's exit-time check-in handshake, so at process exit
   the VM prints `Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in` forever
   (observed 09:03:24 → 09:42:08, then the watchdog killed the orphaned `dart` processes).
   This is the 10th recorded occurrence of the hang class tracked in issue #2122 — the
   previous triage attributed `_waitForExitCode` to `package:test_core`; it is pty2's
   (verified: the symbol exists only in pty2; test_core 0.6.21 has no such isolate).

2. **The teardown gap (repo-owned)** — the repo's PTY teardown paths can leave children
   alive:
   - `FaCliHarness.close()` / `hardKill()` (`test/integration/pty_harness.dart`) send one
     signal (SIGTERM+HUP / SIGKILL), wait ≤5 s for `pty.exitCode`, then **give up silently
     (`onTimeout: () => -1`)** — a child that survives the grace window is leaked.
   - `test/cli/tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` tearDown calls `pty?.kill()` **without
     awaiting the exit at all** — the child here is `dart run example/tui_prototype.dart`,
     whose `dartdev` parent handles SIGTERM and can take seconds to fully die on a loaded
     ARM runner. On a hot run the whole `dart test` process reaches exit while that child
     is still dying → wedged exit (exactly run 43151400571 / PR #2121: all 81 tests green
     in ~30 s, then a 36-min hang).
   - pty2's `kill()` is **once-only** (`if (_killed) return false;`) and `pid` is not
     exposed (upstream left `int get pid` commented out), so the harness **cannot escalate
     to SIGKILL** through the public API even if it wanted to.

3. **The mid-run trigger (upstream, unfixable here)** — in this particular run the VM
   began shutting down MID-RUN (12 suites still queued): the per-suite coverage collector
   (`package:coverage collect` → `getSourceReport`) lost its in-process VM-service
   websocket (`getSourceReport: (-32000) Service connection disposed`, 09:03:13), which
   fails `Engine.run` and starts the shutdown. `isolate.kill` on in-flight suites never
   runs their `tearDown`s, so three suites' live PTY children (`tui_prototype`'s
   `dart run`, `shell_job_countdown`'s fa (4 s into an 8-min test), `ssh_shift_gate`'s fa)
   survived and their `_waitForExitCode` isolates wedged the exit (layer 1). The websocket
   closure itself is the same upstream VM-stall class #2122 tracks; the owner decision
   there stands (accept, self-heals on re-run — the same sha was green twice today:
   08:40 and 06:49).

**Impact**: Any PTY child outliving its test turns a finished `dart test` into a
40-minute zombie job; on tag runs this blocks the release publish (v1.0.735 never
published). Median cost per occurrence: ~37 wasted runner-minutes + a red Quality gate
+ a blocked merge/publish.

**Fix approach** (minimum targeted, root-cause layers 1–2; layer 3 stays upstream):

- Vendor pty2 0.5.7 → `vendor/pty2` and expose `pid` (uncomment upstream's own commented
  getter on all four impls) — the repo-standard patched-fork pattern (`vendor/xterm`,
  `vendor/dart_tui`). Pinned via `pubspec_overrides.yaml` for the root package (test-tree
  consumers only; flutter_app keeps hosted pty2).
- Add `shutdownPty()` in `test/integration/pty_harness.dart`: `kill` → awaited bounded
  grace (FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE-aware) → `Process.killPid(pid, SIGKILL)` escalation →
  awaited bounded wait → **throw loudly** if the child still lives (a leaked child is
  guaranteed to zombie the leg; a loud failure names the culprit instead).
  `FaCliHarness.close()`/`hardKill()` delegate to it.
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` tearDown now awaits `shutdownPty` instead of the

arguments.content:
# Vendored: pty2

- **Upstream**: https://github.com/jtmcdole/termui/tree/main/packages/pty2
  (pub.dev `pty2 0.5.7`, MIT — see LICENSE).
- **Why vendored**: gh-2208 — pty2's `BlockingPseudoTerminal` runs a
  `_waitForExitCode` isolate blocked in a native FFI `waitpid` with no
  timeout. While a PTY child lives, that isolate can neither reach a
  safepoint nor answer the Dart VM's exit-time check-in handshake, so the
  whole `dart test` process wedges forever
  (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in` — CI runs
  43835937617 / v1.0.735 and 43151400571 / PR #2121; tracker issue #2122).
  The PTY test harness (`test/integration/pty_harness.dart`) needs the
  child pid to SIGKILL-escalate when the cooperative `kill()` (SIGTERM +
  SIGHUP, once-only per pty2's `_killed` flag) does not reap the child
  within its grace window — otherwise a leaked child turns the CI leg
  into a 40-minute zombie.
- **Patch vs upstream 0.5.7** (the only diff): the `pid` getter is exposed
  end-to-end — `PtyCore.pid` + `PseudoTerminal.pid` interface members,
  `BasePseudoTerminal.pid`/`PtyCoreUnix.pid` delegating to the existing
  private `_pid`, and `PtyCoreWindows.pid` via `GetProcessId(_hProcess)`
  (upstream's commented-out shape returned the process HANDLE, not the
  pid). `pubspec.yaml`: dropped the upstream `resolution: workspace`
  marker (this repo is not a pub workspace). Everything else is verbatim.
- **Consumers**: the root package only (`pubspec_overrides.yaml`);
  `flutter_app` keeps the hosted 0.5.7 — behavior identical, the patch
  adds getters only.
- **Un-vendor when**: upstream exposes `pid` in a release; bump the
  override back to the hosted constraint and delete this directory.

arguments.content:
### Root Cause

The `PTY/CLI integration (linux, shard 2/3)` leg (run 43835937617, v1.0.735) hung 39 idle minutes until the 40-min watchdog killed it: pty2's `_waitForExitCode` isolate blocks in a native `waitpid` with no timeout, so while ANY PTY child outlives its test, that isolate can never answer the Dart VM's exit-time check-in handshake (`Attempt:N waiting for isolate _waitForExitCode to check in`) and the whole `dart test` process zombies. The repo's teardown paths fed this: `FaCliHarness.close()`/`hardKill()` silently gave up after 5 s, `tui_prototype_snapshot_test` tearDown killed without awaiting, `setup_wizard_portability_test` never killed its PTY children at all, and pty2's once-only `kill()` + unexposed `pid` made SIGKILL escalation impossible. 10th occurrence of the class — tracker #2122.

### Fix

- `vendor/pty2` (patched 0.5.7 fork, `VENDORED.md` documents the diff): exposes `pid` end-to-end (upstream's own commented-out getter); pinned via `pubspec_overrides.yaml` for the root package — flutter_app keeps hosted pty2.
- `test/integration/pty_harness.dart`: new top-level `shutdownPty()` — cooperative kill → awaited grace (FA_PTY_BUDGET_SCALE-aware) → SIGKILL escalation via `Process.killPid` → awaited reap → **loud StateError** if the child still lives; `close()`/`hardKill()` delegate to it; `spawn()` auto-registers an idempotent safety-net close so an early throw can no longer leak a CLI.
- `tui_prototype_snapshot_test.dart` tearDown + `setup_wizard_portability_test.dart` (5 spawn sites) now await reap-or-escalate.

### Test Coverage

- `test/integration/pty_harness_kill_escalation_test.dart` — new: a child trapping SIGTERM+HUP must be dead when `shutdownPty` returns (fails against the old give-up semantics, passes with escalation); hard-path and fast-path pins — PASSED.
- Re-ran the three suites frozen in the crashed shard (`ssh_shift_gate`, `shell_job_countdown_pty`, `resume_tail_grid_pty`) at concurrency 4 — 5/5 PASSED, process exits cleanly.
- Full deterministic suite `dart test --exclude-tags integration`: green (see run log).

### Notes

- No lib/ production code changed; test-tree + vendored test-only dependency only. Pre-commit gate scope unaffected (integration-taged files excluded from the deterministic legs; the new test bin-packs into the PTY/CLI CI shards at runtime like any new integration file).
- Residual (accepted per #2122 owner call): if the VM service dies mid-run while suites hold live mid-test children, the shutdown wedge can still occur — teardowns don't run on `isolate.kill`. This change removes every repo-owned path that leaves a child alive at exit; the mid-run trigger remains upstream.
- `scripts/check_lockfiles.sh` fails locally on `flutter_app/.flutter-plugins-dependencies` (needs `flutter pub get` first) — pre-existing environment gap, untouched by this change; the root `pubspec.lock` is untracked by design, CI regenerates it from the committed `pubspec_overrides.yaml`.
